stemMd: A lecturer argues that a new theory is true because nobody has conclusively disproved it. The argument assumes that

options.label: A
options.textMd: a claim must be true whenever decisive evidence against it is absent.

options.label: D
options.textMd: all theories are easy to test.

explanationMd: Lack of a conclusive disproof is compatible with truth, falsity, or insufficient evidence. The argument needs positive support or an exhaustive test; mere survival of criticism does not establish truth.

distractorRationale.e: The argument concerns evidence, not changing truth.
distractorRationale.d: Ease of testing is not asserted.
distractorRationale.c: The origin of the theory is unspecified.
distractorRationale.b: No claim about critics' honesty appears.
